Displacements in the nodes in the lower surface of the anchor plate were fixed (Figure 10(b)), to provide structural support to the tank boss parts under compression from bolt tightening. Figure 10: (a) Finite element model of the inner tank, and (b) close-up of the FE model of the boss parts and their connection to the tank A bolt load of 15514 N per bolt, for 8 bolts was applied in the model- for load-case 1. The cool-down (i.e. load- case 2) in the tank took place from 300K to 28K in 4 zones starting from the bottom to the top, to simulate the effect of the tank filling up with LH2. An internal pressure of 27.5 bar was applied to the inside of the tank after cool-down. This is 1.8 times higher than the burst pressure (including factor of safety). The reason for this was to understand the limit of this tank geometry. The layup considered was [+55/-55]. Other layups have also been implemented to reduce stresses in plies. This is covered in section 2.5. Figure 11 shows the through-thickness compressive stress profiles in the tank after each load-case: bolt compression, cooldown and internal pressurization. The compressive stresses are seen to be very localized to the area of the boss and value of these stresses (~72 MPa) are within the compressive failure limit published in literature (171 MPa to 200 MPa). More importantly, the addition of internal pressure did not show an increase in compressive stresses around the boss area. This allows us to conclude that the internal pressurization of the tank does not affect the stresses in the boss/flange area. Highest contribution of compressive stress is from bolt loads. Figure 12 shows the maximum stresses along the fiber direction (S11) in the tank arising from each of the 3 load-cases. The peak stresses in the tank, at 326 MPa, are quite low relative to the tensile strength of the tape along the fiber direction (3168 MPa). The analysis shows that there is a lot of margin in this aspect. Figure 13 shows transverse direction stresses (S22), i.e. along the ‘width’ direction of the tape. The stresses are about 41.9 MPa and this is closer to the allowable limit (53 MPa) of the tank along the transverse direction. There is a margin of about 21%, which is reasonable, especially considering that the applied load is 1.7 times higher than the requirement (over and beyond the factor of safety).
